title: Harden blunder audit path handling and local file serving
description:
The blunder audit tooling has a cluster of CodeQL findings around unvalidated filesystem paths and file serving (`py/path-injection` alerts 21-28 and `py/http-response-splitting` alert 20), plus an unflagged network-exposure problem in the same area.

Current behavior:
- `scripts/analysis/blunder_audit.py:429-455` accepts a pasted viewer URL, extracts `game_id`, and passes it to `game_path_for_id()` with no central validation.
- `scripts/analysis/blunder_eval_common.py:110-152` constructs export and ground-truth paths directly from `game_id`.
- `scripts/analysis/blunder_audit_web.py:386-395` serves `/games/{filename}` by joining the request path onto `website/public/games/`, only rejecting obvious `..` and `/` cases.
- `scripts/analysis/blunder_audit_web.py:512` binds the audit web UI to `0.0.0.0`, even though this is a local single-user tool.

This should be fixed as one hardening pass rather than dismissed piecemeal. Suggested scope:
- Add a single validator for export `game_id` values and use it in `game_path_for_id()`, ground-truth helpers, and the URL parser.
- Restrict `/games/` serving to validated export filenames (`game_*.json` / `game_*.json.gz`) instead of ad hoc substring checks.
- Keep content-type generation derived from validated paths only; if needed, stop trusting request-derived names for MIME selection.
- Bind the audit web server to loopback by default (`127.0.0.1`) and keep the printable URL hostname separate if needed.
- Add regression tests for rejected traversal / malformed IDs and for loopback binding.

This is a real fix candidate, not just a dismissal cleanup, because the affected code accepts user-provided URLs and HTTP paths and currently trusts them too far.
